[{"sha":"d7474da72add1470be23a974ff670cff3d995e7f","node_id":"C_kwDOAm1cxNoAKGQ3NDc0ZGE3MmFkZDE0NzBiZTIzYTk3NGZmNjcwY2ZmM2Q5OTVlN2Y","commit":{"author":{"name":"Sayak Kundu","email":"sk.sayakkundu1997@gmail.com","date":"2026-09-30T06:03:04Z"},"committer":{"name":"grs","email":"gsim@redhat.com","date":"2026-10-07T08:29:25Z"},"message":"Bound nesting depth when decoding AMQP compound and described types

The Reader decoded lists, maps, arrays, and described types by recursing
without any limit on nesting depth, so a small deeply nested payload could
exhaust the call stack. Track the current depth on the Reader and reject a
value whose nesting exceeds a fixed maximum (64), covering both the value
path (read_value) and the described-descriptor path (read_constructor).
Adds regression tests alongside the existing compound-count bounds.

Signed-off-by: Sayak Kundu
